Uncertain; may derive from the same root as irto-. Alternatively, per Liukkonen (1999), apud Junttila (2024), borrowed from Baltic *irstan(t)s (compare Lithuanian i̇̀rstąs, participle of i̇̀rti (“to fall apart, crumble, decay; to lapse”)). For the -rst- ~ -rt(t)-, compare karsta, varsta.
Possibly Proto-Finnic *kaila- + -va (compare dialectal Estonian kail (“white-headed cow”)), possibly from Baltic (compare Old Prussian gaylis).
Proto-Finnic *kiili + -iäinen, probably of Baltic origin.
Probably from an onomatopoeic root; kuh- + -ista. Alternatively a Baltic borrowing (compare Latvian kustēt).

parole.significato: a traditional shoe folded from a single piece of leather and with a single shoelace/string
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic [Term?] + -onen, the root borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian kurpe)

parole.significato: to scorch, parch, sear (to burn the surface of)
parole.testo: Possibly a variant of korventaa with contamination from käry, käristä, or simply a derivation from one of the latter. Alternatively a derivation from kärvätä, possibly a Baltic borrowing akin to Lithuanian skrebti.

Proto-Finnic *mala + -o, borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian mala, Lithuanian malá). The original senses are “shore, coast” and “edge, side”. The senses “hole, opening, mouth” and “crack, fissure, gap” are later developments.
Possibly a Baltic loan; compare Lithuanian suktas (“twisted”).

parole.significato: direction (indication of the point toward which an object is moving)

Possibly from Proto-Finnic *vëika- + -eä, if derived from the Baltic root found in Lithuanian veikùs (“quick”).

Formed with the suffix -nko from a root of unknown origin, which has been proposed, among others, to derive from auer (thus from earlier *auderinko),from a Baltic language (compare Lithuanian aušrà (“dawn”)), or according to Saarikivi (2022), possibly from Old Norse Aurvandill. Uncertain, but proposed to be a Baltic loan (whence Lithuanian žaizda (“wound”)), or alternatively possibly from earlier *hagitta and then from Proto-Norse *hagiþō, compare Swedish hejd. Cognate with Karelian haitta.

parole.significato: skirt, base, lap (part of a dress or robe, etc., that hangs below the waist)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hëlma (compare Estonian hõlm), possibly borrowed either from Baltic (compare Lithuanian šelmuo (“ridge (of a roof)”)) or from Proto-Germanic *helmaz (“protective covering”) (compare Old English helm (“helmet, protection, covering”)).

From Proto-Finnic *hämärä, derived from a root hämä-, which may be possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic sámur) or from Baltic. Related to Estonian hämar, Karelian hämärä, Livonian ämār, Veps hämär and Votic hämäre.

parole.significato: thick, dry and hard bark, such as that of a pine
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karna, borrowed either from Baltic *karna- or alternatively Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skarna) (in which case related to English shear and Swedish skära).

parole.significato: to limb, delimb (to remove the branches of a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karcidak, borrowed from Proto-Germanic *skardijaną, or alternatively from Baltic (compare Lithuanian skardyti).

parole.significato: a type of boat used to drag a seine
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karbas, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse karfi), or alternatively and less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kãrbas).

parole.significato: to do, work, suffice, be good enough
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këlbat'ak (compare Estonian kõlbama), borrowed from Pre-Germanic *kelp- (“help”) (from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelb-, *ḱelp- and whence Proto-Germanic *helpaną, compare English help, Swedish hjälpa), or alternatively borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian gelbėti).

parole.significato: to stand, withstand, endure, hold up (to), stand up (to)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kestädäk (compare Estonian kestma), possibly either borrowed from Baltic (compare Lithuanian kę̃sti) or alternatively derived from keski-.
From Proto-Finnic *käki, either a Baltic loanword or alternatively an onomatopoeia. Related to Estonian kägu, Karelian käki, Livonian kä’g, Veps kägi, Votic čako and Northern Sami giehka.

Unknown, but related to Northern Sami luopma. Possibly from luoda. From Proto-Finnic *noodëh (albeit without any known Finnic cognates), either borrowed from Baltic (compare Latvian znots) or alternatively from Proto-Germanic *knōdiz.
From Proto-Finnic *palvodak, possibly borrowed from Baltic. Cognate with Estonian paluma and Livonian pallõ (“to ask for”). Alternatively related to Erzya паламс (palams, “kiss”).

parole.significato: sail; (colloquial) rag, sheet (piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive th…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purjëh, probably borrowed from Proto-Germanic *buriz (“favourable wind”), or alternatively and less likely from Baltic (compare Lithuanian burė, Latvian bura). The Baltic words have also sometimes been proposed to be Finnic loans.
From Proto-Finnic *rakja, borrowed from either a Germanic or alternatively a Baltic language.
From Proto-Finnic *virta, borrowed from either Proto-Slavic *vьrtъ or a Baltic cognate thereof.
